title: Prospective study on emergency diagnostics of periprosthetic joint infection of the lower extremity
summary:
The primary objective of this study is the development and internal validation of an emergency department-oriented diagnostic approach for the early assessment of probable or confirmed periprosthetic joint infection based on clinical, laboratory, imaging, and synovial parameters.

Primary hypothesis: A combination of clinical findings routinely obtained in the emergency department, laboratory parameters, and imaging and synovial examinations enables reliable prediction of the presence of probable or confirmed periprosthetic joint infection according to the EBJIS classification, even in the acute setting.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to other internal prosthetic devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name:
Within the framework of this study, clinical, laboratory, and imaging parameters obtained during emergency department assessment will be prospectively collected in patients with suspected periprosthetic joint infection of the lower extremity.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥18 years
Lower extremity prosthesis
Clinical suspicion of PJI
Written consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years
- Inability to give informed consent and no legal representative available
- Refusal to participate in the study
- No endoprosthesis in the target joint
- Inability to establish a definitive clinical diagnosis or to collect the necessary routine data (e.g., in cases of immediate transfer to another facility without access to relevant medical records)
